title: Domain Name Resolution, RFC 1035 Wire Queries, Record Types & Caching
topic: Domain Names, DNS Records (A/AAAA/CNAME/NS), Recursive vs. Iterative Resolution, Caching
learning_objectives: Observe real RFC 1035 DNS queries and responses transmitted over UDP.
Distinguish A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, and NS records and recursive vs. iterative resolution.
Measure and explain the latency difference between uncached lookups and cached DNS responses.

concept_explanation.title: Hierarchical Namespace & DNS Records
concept_explanation.summary: DNS maps human-readable domain names to IP addresses and service metadata using a distributed hierarchy (Root -> TLD -> Authoritative nameservers).
key_points: Common record types: A (IPv4), AAAA (IPv6), CNAME (alias), NS (nameserver), MX (mail exchanger).
Standard DNS queries use UDP (typically port 53) for single-packet speed, falling back to TCP for large or truncated responses.

concept_explanation.title: Recursive vs. Iterative Resolution & TTL Caching
concept_explanation.summary: Stub resolvers send recursive queries to a local recursive resolver, which iteratively queries Root, TLD, and Authoritative servers and caches the answer for TTL seconds.
key_points: TTL (Time To Live) controls how long resolvers cache a DNS record before re-querying.
Cached lookups avoid upstream round trips and dramatically reduce resolution latency.

experiment.title: Run Offline-Safe RFC 1035 DNS Query/Response & Cache Latency Experiment
experiment.instructions: Executes a controlled localhost RFC 1035 UDP DNS responder and client. Sends a real DNS A-record query twice — first uncached (simulating recursive resolution latency) and second cached — while capturing real UDP wire packets on loopback.
required_setup: Localhost UDP loopback (100% offline — requires zero Internet connectivity)
Phase 4 libpcap capture helper for real UDP DNS packet capture
execution_steps: Run 'Local RFC 1035 DNS Query + Cache Comparison' to capture actual binary DNS query/response packets over UDP.
Inspect the measured uncached vs. cached response times, transaction IDs, record type (A), TTL, and returned IPv4 answer.
Optionally run 'System Resolver Lookup (localhost)' to inspect OS resolver behavior.

supported_scenarios.label: 1. Local RFC 1035 DNS Query & Cache Comparison (Offline-Safe)
supported_scenarios.description: Sends real RFC 1035 binary DNS A-record queries over UDP loopback (uncached vs. cached) with packet capture.

expected_observations: Real UDP DNS query and response packets are captured on loopback with matching DNS Transaction IDs.
The DNS response includes an A record answer and TTL value.
The cached lookup completes measurably faster than the initial uncached lookup.
observation_caveats: The offline-safe DNS lab runs an authoritative local responder on an ephemeral localhost UDP port (not public port 53) so it works reliably without Internet access.
NetBox never claims external Internet DNS packets were captured unless they actually appear in the capture.

questions.prompt: Why does standard DNS primarily use UDP rather than TCP for routine A/AAAA queries?
options: Most DNS queries and responses fit in a single datagram, avoiding TCP's 3-way handshake latency overhead.
questions.rubric_summary: UDP avoids 3-way handshake overhead for small single-packet request/response exchanges.
questions.explanation: A typical DNS query/response fits cleanly in one UDP datagram, completing in 1 RTT instead of TCP's handshake + request + teardown overhead.

questions.prompt: What is the role of the TTL (Time To Live) field inside a DNS resource record?
options: Maximum number of router hops the packet can traverse.
Number of seconds a resolver may cache the DNS record before re-querying upstream.
Maximum length of a domain name in bytes.
The port number of the recursive resolver.
questions.rubric_summary: DNS record TTL specifies cache lifetime in seconds (distinct from IP header hop TTL).
questions.explanation: DNS TTL (in seconds) tells caching resolvers how long to reuse an answer before expiring it. Do not confuse DNS record TTL with IPv4 header hop-limit TTL.

questions.prompt: Distinguish a recursive DNS query from an iterative DNS query.
questions.rubric_summary: Recursive asks resolver to return the final answer; iterative returns best-known answer or referral to next nameserver.
questions.explanation: In a recursive query, the client asks the resolver to chase down and return the final IP answer. In an iterative query, a nameserver replies with either the answer or a referral to the next authoritative server.
